title: Harbor and Clock
premise: In the waning months of a collapsing republic, Zephyrine Sterling carries diplomatic codes between a besieged coastal town and a government that no longer answers. When an advancing army requisitions the harbor town and seizes the ledger holding every name of those promised safe passage, Zephyrine discovers their own name among them — and the name of Ilse Marchetti, a lighthouse keeper's daughter now declared enemy, to whom they swore a peacetime promise. Hunted by both sides, Zephyrine gathers a found family of smugglers, defrocked clerks, and deserters to steal the ledger back and honor the promise before the armistice is signed — or quietly never is. The book ends with the armistice signed on paper but betrayed in practice; Zephyrine delivers Ilse to neutral water at terrible cost, keeps the ledger's names alive by memory alone, and chooses justice outside any law that failed them.
about_author: Silas Kavanagh is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters from occupied port towns. They write from a house above a decommissioned lighthouse, where the foghorn still sounds once a year, on the anniversary of an armistice nobody celebrates.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Zephyrine Sterling crosses a rain-soaked checkpoint with codes sewn into a coat lining, measuring every object in their satchel by what it would cost if found. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: wary competence masking dread as the republic visibly rots around them.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: In the harbor customs house, clerk Odile Ferrand shows Zephyrine the ledger guaranteeing passage for two hundred people — including Ilse Marchetti, the lighthouse keeper's daughter Zephyrine promised in peacetime to protect. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: tenderness rekindled and immediately shadowed by foreboding.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: At dawn, army officers seal the town, commandeer the customs house, and confiscate the ledger as 'enemy documentation.' Odile is arrested protesting. POV: Odile. Beat: shock curdling into helpless fury.

chapters.title: The Salt Road
chapters.summary: Zephyrine flees through salt marshes with smuggler Bram Voss, who knows which channels the patrols don't. They argue about whether promises survive borders. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: reluctant alliance formed under threat.

chapters.title: Enemy by Declaration
chapters.summary: A proclamations poster names Ilse Marchetti an enemy collaborator. Zephyrine learns she has gone silent from the lighthouse. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: guilt sharpened into resolve — the promise now has a deadline.

chapters.title: The Deserters' Chapel
chapters.summary: Bram leads Zephyrine to a ruined chapel sheltering deserters from both armies, led by former schoolteacher Anselm Rey. They trade news: the ledger sits in the requisitioned customs house under a captain who burns what he cannot use. POV: Anselm. Beat: fragile community offered, cautiously accepted.

chapters.title: Odile's Cell
chapters.summary: Odile, interrogated but unbroken, memorizes ledger pages before guards can burn them, hiding names inside psalm rhythms. POV: Odile. Beat: quiet heroism; memory as resistance.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Dark
chapters.summary: Zephyrine reaches the lighthouse and finds it dark, Ilse hiding in the lamp room, her father taken. Their reunion is fierce, distrustful, and tender. POV: Ilse. Beat: love complicated by betrayal — Zephyrine's republic wrote her name into the ledger and then let it be seized.

chapters.title: Terms of the Armistice
chapters.summary: Rumors spread that an armistice will be signed within weeks; amnesty lists are being drafted from the very ledgers now in army hands. If your name isn't on paper, you don't exist. POV: Anselm. Beat: stakes crystallize — time is running out.

chapters.title: Mapping the Customs House
chapters.summary: Bram bribes a dockhand for the building's rotations; Odile's smuggled note confirms the ledger survives, locked in the captain's map room. POV: Bram. Beat: hope with teeth; the plan takes shape.

chapters.title: The Cost of Carrying
chapters.summary: Ilse refuses to hide while others risk themselves; she reveals she kept her own copy of half the ledger pages — her father's doing — but the other half burned. POV: Ilse. Beat: pride and grief braided together.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Fish Market
chapters.summary: A chapel deserter sells information for rations; soldiers raid the fish market meeting. Zephyrine escapes, but Anselm is taken. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: trust shattered; the found family bleeds.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Anselm, beaten, gives up nothing but misdirection, buying three days. The young officer questioning him begins to doubt his own orders. POV: Anselm. Beat: dignity under cruelty; a crack in the enemy's certainty.

chapters.title: The Captain's Dinner
chapters.summary: Bram infiltrates a requisition banquet as a wine merchant, confirming the ledger's location and learning the armistice may be delayed indefinitely — some names are meant to be erased. POV: Bram. Beat: cold clarity; this is erasure, not bureaucracy.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Around a driftwood fire, the group debates whether one promise justifies risking two hundred names. Ilse argues memory outlasts paper; Zephyrine finally stops carrying guilt like cargo and speaks plainly of love. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: emotional midpoint turned toward commitment.

chapters.title: Night of Fog
chapters.summary: The heist: Odile's guard rotation knowledge, Bram's forged passes, Ilse cutting the harbor lights. They reach the map room — and find the ledger already crated for burning. POV: rotating close-third. Beat: breathless tension.

chapters.title: Fire in the Map Room
chapters.summary: Cornered, they set a diversionary fire, and the doubting young officer — recognizing Anselm's mercy earlier — looks away at the crucial moment. They carry the ledger out through smoke. POV: the young officer, briefly. Beat: an enemy choosing conscience.

chapters.title: The Long Pier
chapters.summary: Chased along the breakwater, Bram stays behind to hold the gate and is captured. The ledger reaches the boat, but the escape route is compromised. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: sacrifice; victory priced in blood.

chapters.title: Armistice, Signed or Not
chapters.summary: Word arrives: the armistice is signed — but the amnesty list excludes 'irregular persons,' meaning everyone in the ledger. The law has spoken, and it has lied. POV: Odile. Beat: bitter vindication; justice must come from elsewhere.

chapters.title: Neutral Water
chapters.summary: In fog, Zephyrine delivers Ilse to a neutral tramp steamer — the promise kept. Ilse asks Zephyrine to come; Zephyrine stays to see the other names through. POV: Ilse. Beat: heartbreak as fulfillment; love proven by letting go.

chapters.title: The Reading of Names
chapters.summary: In the chapel, the survivors read all two hundred names aloud and copy them into new hands — Odile's memory, Ilse's half-copy, the rescued ledger — so no authority can again make them disappear. POV: Anselm. Beat: mourning transfigured into covenant.

chapters.title: Harbor and Clock
chapters.summary: Years later, Zephyrine tends the relit lighthouse, keeping time not by clocks but by tides and the annual reading of names. A letter arrives from Ilse across the water. Justice was never delivered by the law — only carried, hand to hand. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: hard-won peace; memory as the only honest state.
